title: Research fast-topo-router for OMP integration fit
description:
Research completed 2026-11-21 against upstream commit 5038df93e26ce67a9d04b4180074a87a366fde50.

Findings: fast-topo-router is a TypeScript context compaction and typed routing gateway for coding agents, including OMP; it is not an OMP agent-topology loader. CodeCompactor extracts TS/TSX declarations and relative import edges into bounded XML. Jev or Ollama then answers a caller-supplied scalar schema; MCP exposes local-only topo_compact and network-capable topo_route. OMP setup is a manual MCP server entry, outside this repo’s current portable overlay/installer contract. Its own docs state outputs are advisory and cannot waive required checks; token-savings figures are source-reported character/4 estimates, not billed-token or task-speedup measurements. MIT license. At check time: 0 stars/forks, no releases/tags, last push 2026-09-19; maturity/maintenance evidence is limited.

Decision: no code branch or integration work now; there is no concrete implementation scope. Revisit only if optional MCP registration becomes a product requirement.

Sources (pinned commit): README.md lines 5-19, 59-72; documents/blueprint.md lines 8-13, 53-63, 119-129; documents/integration-mcp.md lines 38-58; src/compactors/code-compactor.ts lines 193-203; src/mcp/server.ts lines 102-112, 114-150.
acceptance_criteria: Source-backed summary recorded; OMP topology-vs-MCP fit assessed; branch decision documented; no code changes, install, or external issue created.
close_reason: Completed source-backed research against upstream commit 5038df93e26ce67a9d04b4180074a87a366fde50. fast-topo-router is an optional code-context MCP gateway, not an OMP topology loader; no code change or isolated branch is warranted now. Full findings and pinned source locators are recorded in the issue.

title: Port topology install and remove behavior to Rust
description: Migrate existing bin/omp-topology behavior to Rust while preserving supported list/install/remove flows and safety contracts: ownership manifests, compatible removal of existing manifests, backups, atomic writes, symlink/path protections, dry-run, idempotency, default target resolution through `omp config path`, and explicit `--agent-dir`/`--skills-dir` options. The legacy installer has no `--profile` option; named OMP profiles require an explicitly resolved `--agent-dir` until the separate profile-lifecycle feature. Evaluate yaml-edit as the initial candidate for lossless YAML merge against current comment-preservation/unknown-key behavior; select a maintained round-trip crate only after a focused parity spike. Keep merge logic direct and auditable; do not build a generic framework.
design:
### YAML engine research and decision

As of 2026-11-22, `yaml-edit` 0.3.6 is the leading Rust candidate. Its [API docs](https://docs.rs/yaml-edit/0.3.6/yaml_edit/) describe lossless CST editing that preserves comments, whitespace, and formatting; its [design](https://github.com/jelmer/yaml-edit/blob/main/DESIGN.md) states that unedited round trips are byte-identical. Its `migrate::to_yaml_1_2` helper preserves YAML 1.1 scalar meanings while rewriting ambiguous spellings (documented example: `yes` -> `true`). This matters because the current topology fixture contains `autoParallel: on`, which yq treats as boolean true.

Prefer a pure-Rust round-trip path over a runtime yq dependency, but do not finalize the crate until an end-to-end Rust install regression proves existing comments/unknown values survive and `autoParallel: on` retains boolean semantics. If it fails, reopen the decision with evidence rather than silently adding yq or a custom YAML parser. First implementation slice: add a test-first CLI install contract in isolated temp agent/state directories.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Existing CLI behavior and user-visible safety contracts have Rust contract coverage, including comments/unknown YAML values and legacy manifests. - [ ] Round-trip crate selection is evidence-based and documented; no custom parser or unnecessary wrapper abstraction. - [ ] Repeated install/remove, dry-run, collision, symlink, backup, and edit-aware removal paths are covered. - [ ] Non-trivial merge/path algorithms state expected Big-O and avoid repeated avoidable scans/copies.
- [x] Legacy target selection is covered: `omp config path` by default and explicit `--agent-dir`/`--skills-dir` overrides; the Rust parity port and README do not claim installer-level `--profile` support.
close_reason: Rust parity port completed with verified CLI contracts, safe filesystem behavior, performance fixes, and clean Python-to-Rust cutover.

title: Add topology sources, profile registry, aliases, and lifecycle commands
description: Add explicit source and profile management to the Rust CLI. Support GitHub sources (for example github:OWNER/REPO with --ref) and local paths; resolve/record source and commit/ref in a local XDG state registry, while existing per-target ownership manifests remain authoritative for safe removal. Add profiles list, status, update, and self-update commands; --json; explicit --profile and --alias NAME to identify a managed installation, with status/update/remove addressing that alias. Keep a profile picker opt-in if included; never silently target every profile. Retain --dry-run, --agent-dir, --skills-dir, and existing topology selection. The registry must contain no OAuth credentials or other secrets. Document that models, plugins, and slash commands may need installation per profile; verify current OMP auth semantics before claiming exact OAuth refresh-token behavior, and advise fresh OAuth authentication per profile rather than copying tokens. Long-haul/performance coverage: repeated install/update/remove cycles against growing synthetic profile/registry/backup state, with deterministic scale tests and an opt-in or scheduled soak/benchmark; no flaky wall-clock threshold in ordinary unit tests. State growth and backup-retention behavior must be explicit and tested.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] GitHub and local sources, explicit refs, profile discovery, registry status, alias-based lifecycle, JSON output, and update flows are documented and tested. - [ ] Installs remain explicitly scoped to a selected profile; no implicit all-profile install or unsafe force behavior. - [ ] Registry stores source metadata only and never credentials; auth/setup documentation is checked against current OMP behavior. - [ ] Repeated-cycle/scale coverage detects pathological state growth and performance regressions representative of long-lived use; routine CI remains deterministic.
notes:
Main technical decisions for implementation:
- Keep `--profile` and `--alias` distinct: `--profile` selects the OMP profile; `--alias` names the managed registry entry. Both may be supplied on install. `--profile` and `--agent-dir` are mutually exclusive; alias alone cannot choose a target on first install. Lifecycle by alias must never affect other profiles. Default aliases derive from explicit profile (`default` for ambient default), or custom agent-dir basename; collisions require explicit `--alias`.
- `profiles list` discovers existing default/named OMP profile directories and shows whether each is managed. Do not call `omp config path` for a nonexistent profile while discovering; OMP creates profile directories on demand.
- GitHub source fetch uses `git` with argument arrays (no shell), resolves and records a full commit; local source records an overlay digest. Git is available in the pinned Rust Docker image; give an actionable error when missing. Keep immutable source cache bounded: retain registry-referenced commits plus at most 10 unreferenced cache entries per source, prune only after successful operations. Dry-run must not persist cache/state.
- Registry remains XDG-private, atomic, locked, and metadata-only; per-target manifest remains removal authority. Keep the newest 10 install/remove backups per agent state directory, pruning only after successful mutation.
- `--json` emits one document to stdout; errors stay on stderr. Updates never force-overwrite user edits.
- Self-update and the later bootstrap installer must share one signature contract: signed `SHA256SUMS` using RSA/SHA-256; public PEM key committed, private key only in a GitHub Actions secret; verify signature and asset checksum before replacing/installing. Research cross-platform OpenSSL verification and document the required release secret; never allow unsigned fallback.
Installed-binary integration requirement: registry/state operations must still work when the binary has no topology checkout beside it. Keep source-tree discovery (`repo_root`) separate from the state-root safety anchor; compute a stable existing anchor (checkout root when available, otherwise executable parent) for XDG containment checks. `--source` selects topology data only and must not relocate the user registry or manifest state. Without an available bundled checkout, no-source list/install should return an actionable `--source` instruction; status/profiles/remove must remain usable.
Alias collision semantics: idempotent install is allowed only when an existing alias still maps to the same absolute agent_dir and topology. Refuse reuse of an alias for a different target/topology, and refuse a second alias for an agent_dir already managed by another alias; `profiles list` and status-by-profile rely on an unambiguous profile-to-alias mapping.
